newsitem.title: CHINA: H.K. gold closes sharply lower on heavy selling.
newsitem.headline: H.K. gold closes sharply lower on heavy selling.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed sharply lower on Monday after heavy selling and long-liquidation from Asian investors, extending its slump to 12-year lows last week, and dealers said prices would head lower.
Bullion ended at US$318.50/319.00 an ounce, down from the local opening of US$321.80/322.30 and London's US$324.25/75 close on Friday.

"Some local players were staying away in view of golds weakness and sentiment was generally seen bearish in the short term," a senior gold dealer said. "We don't see the bottom yet. The target would be US$315-316 levels."
Local gold ended HK$55 lower at HK$2,952 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Society rose from -6.00 on Saturday to -5.00 on Monday.
